acceptance_criteria: New outbound failure rows preserve stable bounded code, stage, delivery mutation state, retry disposition, attempt accounting, timestamps, and evidence coverage across restart and recovery reads.
No normal outbound failure row, health response, log, alert, or operator projection persists raw exception prose, identity, content, or provider payload.
Pre-I/O denial, definitive rejection, ambiguous handoff, and crash-in-flight remain distinct and status/evidence contradictions fail closed.
Legacy rows remain explicitly unclassified and are never assigned stable meaning by parsing prose.
retry_count gains precise logical-attempt and provider-submission semantics with production readers and writers, or is removed through a safe migration.
Runbook guidance uses a supported bounded diagnostic view rather than raw error inspection.
blast_radius: Outbound durability schema and migrations, agent and chat send transitions, pending draining and restart recovery, health and operator diagnostics, incident grouping, runbook procedures, retention, and transport error consumers.

falsifier_or_remaining_gap: The finding would be falsified if exact main persisted a bounded typed failure record through outbound transition and recovery reads, kept raw exception prose out of the machine contract, and defined real logical-attempt and provider-submission accounting. Exact source disproves those conditions. Implementation must still prove migration, restart, status-evidence coherence, legacy unknown coverage, privacy, and supported redacted diagnostics.
impact: Recovery and operators cannot distinguish pre-I/O denial, definitive rejection, ambiguous provider handoff, crash-in-flight, or replay ownership. Raw provider prose becomes durable privacy and compatibility debt, while false ambiguity and nonexistent attempt accounting weaken safe recovery.
